q: Is there a correct way to structure an edit?
a: There's no single right order. Rough first, then trim: lay every usable take on the timeline in order, cut away what you don't need, then tighten each edit; easy to follow but you handle a lot twice. Three-point editing: watch each clip in the Source monitor, mark only the part you want and drop just that in; less cleanup later, more decisions up front. Mixing the two is normal; try both on a short project.

q: Does the Resolve workflow change what the editing tools do?
a: No: the Resolve workflow (Settings ▸ Workflow, the fork's default) changes the keyboard preset and some words on screen (Sequence becomes Timeline, Project panel becomes Media Pool), not what the tools do. Every command can also be run by its id from the command palette, the control channel or MCP.

q: How do I split a clip into two?
a: Cut at the playhead with Add Edit (`sequence.addEdit`): Cmd+K in the Premiere preset, Cmd+B in the Resolve preset (Cmd is Ctrl on Linux and Windows); it cuts the targeted tracks. Add Edit to All Tracks cuts every track. Or pick the razor tool (`tool.razor`: C in Premiere, B in Resolve), click the clip where you want the cut, and go back to the selection tool (V in Premiere, A in Resolve).

q: How do I remove a range between In and Out?
a: Delete (`edit.clear`) removes the selected clips and leaves a gap; Ripple Delete (`edit.rippleDelete`, Shift+Delete) removes them and closes it. With In and Out set on the timeline, Lift (`sequence.lift`) removes the range and leaves a gap, Extract (`sequence.extract`) removes it and closes the gap; they're on ; and ' in the Premiere preset and in the Timeline menu or command palette in the Resolve preset.

q: How do I open a clip in the Source monitor and mark it?
a: Three-point editing sets three of Source In, Source Out, Timeline In and Timeline Out; Revolution works out the fourth. Double-click a clip in the Project panel / Media Pool to open it in the Source monitor, press I at the start of the part you want and O at the end, put the playhead where it should go, switch on the target tracks, then Insert (comma in Premiere, F9 in Resolve) or Overwrite (period, F10).

q: What are the four points in three-point editing?
a: Three-point editing sets three of Source In, Source Out, Timeline In and Timeline Out; Revolution works out the fourth. Double-click a clip in the Project panel / Media Pool to open it in the Source monitor, press I at the start of the part you want and O at the end, put the playhead where it should go, switch on the target tracks, then Insert (comma in Premiere, F9 in Resolve) or Overwrite (period, F10).

q: and if I want everything after it to stay where it is?
a: Use Overwrite instead of Insert: it replaces whatever is under the new clip and moves nothing.

q: What do J, K and L do?
a: L plays forward, and each extra press doubles the speed (2×, 4×, up to 8×); K stops; J plays backward, doubling the same way. Space plays or pauses at normal speed, and the Left / Right arrow keys step one frame at a time once you're close. The keys act on the monitor you last clicked.

q: How do I trim an edit point with the keyboard?
a: Select an edit point (click it, or Trim Edit `trim.edit`, Shift+T in Premiere, for the nearest one). Toggle Trim Type (`trim.toggleType`, Ctrl+T) cycles ripple, rolling or ripple on one side. Alt+Left / Alt+Right (`trim.backward` / `trim.forward`) move it one frame; add Shift for several. A rolling edit keeps the length, a ripple shifts everything after. Undo puts the whole trim back in one step.

q: What is a multicam clip?
a: Multicam puts several cameras of one moment in one clip with angles, so you watch them side by side and switch while playing. Make it with Clip ▸ Create Multi-Camera Source Sequence (`clip.createMulticam`), lining clips up by In / Out, timecode, a marker or audio. Put it on the timeline, switch the Program monitor to the multicam view (`multicam.toggleView`, Shift+0 in Premiere), press 0 to record and play, then click an angle or press 1–9 to cut. Press 0 again to finish: one undo step.

q: How do I switch multicam angles from a script?
a: `multicam.cut` and `multicam.switchAngle` take a `camera` number (1-based) or an `angle` (0-based). Ctrl+1–9 (`multicam.cutToCamera1` …) add a cut at the playhead and show that camera from there.

q: What are the V1 and A1 buttons on the track headers?
a: Each track header has two switches: the source patch (V1 / A1 next to the track) chooses where the Source monitor's video and audio land on Insert / Overwrite; the track target (the track's name) chooses which tracks the keyboard works on. `timeline.setTargeting` sets one; `timeline.toggleAllVideoTargets` / `toggleAllAudioTargets` (and the source-patch toggles) switch all at once.

q: How do I target all audio tracks at once?
a: Each track header has two switches: the source patch (V1 / A1 next to the track) chooses where the Source monitor's video and audio land on Insert / Overwrite; the track target (the track's name) chooses which tracks the keyboard works on. `timeline.setTargeting` sets one; `timeline.toggleAllVideoTargets` / `toggleAllAudioTargets` (and the source-patch toggles) switch all at once.

q: In Resolve I'd set the track destination controls. How do I do that in Revolution?
a: Use the source patch switches (V1 / A1) on the left of the track headers for where Insert / Overwrite land, and the track target switch for which tracks the keyboard acts on.

q: How do I select the next clip with the keyboard?
a: Select Clip at Playhead (`timeline.selectClipAtPlayhead`), then the next or previous clip (`timeline.selectNextClip` / `selectPrevClip`). Then nudge it a frame left or right (`timeline.nudgeLeft` / `nudgeRight`, or up / down a track), slip it to show an earlier or later part of its source (`timeline.slipLeft` / `slipRight`), or slide it so its neighbours trim (`timeline.slideLeft` / `slideRight`); `…5` versions move five frames. Each press is one undo step.

Then nudge it a frame left or right (`timeline.nudgeLeft` / `nudgeRight`, or up / down a track), slip it to show an earlier or later part of its source (`timeline.slipLeft` / `slipRight`), or slide it so its neighbours trim (`timeline.slideLeft` / `slideRight`); `…5` versions move five frames. Each press is one undo step.

q: How do I jump to the start of the selected clip?
a: Step a frame (`playhead.stepForward` / `stepBack`), five (`…5`) or any number (`playhead.step`); jump to the next or previous edit on the targeted tracks (`playhead.nextEdit` / `prevEdit`) or any track (`…AnyTrack`); go to the selected clip's start or end (`playhead.selectedClipStart` / `selectedClipEnd`), the sequence's start or end, or an exact time with `playhead.set`.

q: How do I move the playhead to an exact time from a script?
a: Step a frame (`playhead.stepForward` / `stepBack`), five (`…5`) or any number (`playhead.step`); jump to the next or previous edit on the targeted tracks (`playhead.nextEdit` / `prevEdit`) or any track (`…AnyTrack`); go to the selected clip's start or end (`playhead.selectedClipStart` / `selectedClipEnd`), the sequence's start or end, or an exact time with `playhead.set`.

q: What do In and Out points control?
a: Mark In / Mark Out (`markers.markIn` / `markOut`) set the range Lift, Extract, export and render work on. Mark Clip marks the clip under the playhead on the targeted tracks, Mark Selection the selected clips. Clear with `markers.clearIn`, `clearOut` or `clearInOut` (Alt+X); jump with `markers.goToIn` / `goToOut`.

q: How do I name and colour a marker?
a: Press M (`markers.add`) for a marker at the playhead; open it (`markers.edit`) for a name, comment, colour or duration. Jump with `markers.goNext` / `goPrev`, filter by colour (`markers.filterColors`), clear one (`markers.clearCurrent`) or all (`markers.clearAll`). Range markers cover a stretch: Add Range Marker (`markers.addRange`, one second) or over In to Out (`markers.addRangeInOut`). Chapter and flash cue markers are for players.
